value.name: decides to drive to Cherry Hill
value.description: Asha leaves on foot with a folder and, before fully voicing the decision to herself, chooses to drive to Cherry Hill instead of returning to the office.
evidence: She walked the two blocks to the lot with the folder still under her arm, set it on the passenger seat next to her bag, and pulled the keys out before she had decided in any sentence she could have said aloud that she was driving to Cherry Hill instead of back to the office.

value.name: drives across the bridge
value.description: Asha drives onto the bridge toward New Jersey, ignoring unanswered calls as she crosses the river.
evidence: The wipers cleared a thin grit from the windshield; she took the ramp for the bridge and let the unanswered calls sit in her pocket the whole way across the river.

value.name: ignores phone calls
value.description: Her phone buzzes, but Asha refuses to answer and decides the caller can wait or go unheard.
evidence: Her phone buzzed twice against her hip near the Haddonfield exit and she did not reach for it; whoever was calling could be returned from a curb in Cherry Hill, or not at all

value.name: rehearses Claire's address
value.description: Asha keeps driving while mentally repeating Claire's address from memory and comparing it to how she reads case captions.
evidence: She watched the exit signs instead, reading Claire's address back to herself from memory the way she read case captions

value.name: loses track of work and rent
value.description: After driving for nearly an hour, Asha realizes she has not thought about the Hatcher file or Friday's rent.
evidence: noticed somewhere past the Cherry Hill Mall that she had been driving for almost an hour without thinking once about the Hatcher file or the rent due Friday

value.name: enters quiet neighborhood streets
value.description: Asha reaches the numbered streets in Cherry Hill, where the houses are quiet and set back behind leafless hedges, and she slows down at each cross street.
evidence: The numbered streets when they came were quieter than she had expected, low brick houses set back behind hedges that had already lost their leaves, and she slowed at each cross stree
